qt: to the Commission Loucas Fourlas (PPE) Subject:

Plans for the British bases to instal new antennae and build new infrastructure in the Akrotiri area raise serious questions concerning protection of public health and the environment. The local authorities have expressed concerns about the scale of the project, the adequacy of the information provided to them and the potential effects of the operation of the new installations. The issue of the antennae is of particular importance given the need to ensure a high level of protection for local inhabitants and the natural environment. The special status of the British bases cannot entail a reduced level of protection for Cypriot and European citizens living in nearby areas. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it consider the planned installations to be compatible with the obligations stemming from the applicable EU environmental acquis?
Does it have any data on the potential impact of the new antennae on public health and the protected natural environment in the area?
What steps does it intend to take, within its remit, to ensure that there is full transparency, that information is provided to affected communities and that European citizens are properly protected?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) According to Article 355.5.b Treaty on the Functioning of the EU, during the UK’s membership in the EU, ‘the Treaties [did] not apply to the United Kingdom Sovereign Base Areas (SBA) of Akrotiri and Dhekelia in Cyprus, except to the extent necessary to ensure the implementation of the arrangements set out in the Protocol No. 3 on the Sovereign Base Areas of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland in Cyprus’1. Such arrangements did not include environmental law. Following the withdrawal of the UK from the EU, the Protocol relating to the UK SBAs annexed to the EU-UK Withdrawal Agreement ensures that EU law, in the areas stipulated in Protocol 3 on the SBAs, continues to apply in the SBAs. This primarily covers customs, taxation, duty relief, social security, agriculture, fisheries and veterinary and phytosanitary rules, border control, and administrative cooperation. No environmental provisions are included. The UK established an SBA Environmental Department in 2002 in recognition of new and impeding environmental legislation to which the Administration of the SBAs has legal and policy responsibilities2. In accordance with the UK 1960 Declaration on the Administration of the SBAs, the SBA Administration seeks to replicate as far as possible the legislation of the Republic of Cyprus, and this also applies to environmental legislation. The SBA Administration is also a signatory to many International Conventions and thus has an obligation to demonstrate good environmental Stewardship of the Bases. As EU environmental law is not applicable in the SBAs, the Commission is not in a position to intervene.
